import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Dean's conjecture on cycles of length divisible by `k`

*References:*
- [arxiv/2605.02731](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.02731)
  **Existence of cycles of length divisible by 3 or 4**
  by *Ilkyoo Choi, Hojin Chu, Ringi Kim, Boram Park*, where this is Conjecture 1.1.
- [De88] Dean, N., Open problem, in Cycles and Rays. (1988).
- [DeLeSa93] Dean, N. and Lesniak, L. and Saito, A., Cycles of length 0 modulo 4 in graphs.
  Discrete Math. (1993), 133--139.
- [ChSa94] Chen, G. and Saito, A., Graphs with a cycle of length divisible by three.
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (1994), 277--292.
-/

open SimpleGraph

namespace Arxiv.«2605.02731»

/--
**Conjecture 1.1 (Dean, 1988).** For every integer $k \geq 3$, every finite simple graph with
minimum degree at least $k$ contains a cycle whose length is divisible by $k$.

A cycle has length at least `3`, so the divisor is never `0` and the statement is not
satisfied for a trivial reason. `SimpleGraph.minDegree` is `0` on a graph with no vertices and
on a graph with no edges, so the hypothesis excludes both.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem dean_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (k : ℕ), 3 ≤ k → ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
      (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj], k ≤ G.minDegree →
        ∃ m ∈ G.cycleLengths, k ∣ m := by
  sorry

/--
The case $k = 5$. This is the only case of the conjecture that is still open.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem dean_conjecture.variants.five :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
      [DecidableRel G.Adj], 5 ≤ G.minDegree → ∃ m ∈ G.cycleLengths, 5 ∣ m := by
  sorry

/--
The case $k = 3$, proved by Chen and Saito [ChSa94].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem dean_conjecture.variants.three {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hG : 3 ≤ G.minDegree) :
    ∃ m ∈ G.cycleLengths, 3 ∣ m := by
  sorry

/--
The case $k = 4$, proved by Dean, Lesniak and Saito [DeLeSa93].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem dean_conjecture.variants.four {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hG : 4 ≤ G.minDegree) :
    ∃ m ∈ G.cycleLengths, 4 ∣ m := by
  sorry

/--
The cases $k \geq 6$, proved by Liu, Ma and Zhao (2026). With [ChSa94] and [DeLeSa93] this
leaves `dean_conjecture.variants.five` as the only open case.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem dean_conjecture.variants.six_le {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] {k : ℕ}
    (hk : 6 ≤ k) (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hG : k ≤ G.minDegree) :
    ∃ m ∈ G.cycleLengths, k ∣ m := by
  sorry

/-- A graph with no edges has minimum degree `0`, so the hypothesis of the conjecture rules it
out. This is a check that the hypothesis carries weight. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem minDegree_bot_eq_zero : (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 5)).minDegree = 0 := by
  decide

/-- The complete graph on four vertices has minimum degree `3`, so it is one of the graphs the
case `k = 3` applies to. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem minDegree_top_fin_four : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 4)).minDegree = 3 := by
  decide

end Arxiv.«2605.02731»

findings.description: The module bibliography lists `[De88]` as “Open problem, in Cycles and Rays. (1988).” Cycles and Rays is a 1990 volume. The cited arXiv paper instead references Dean's “Which graphs are pancyclic modulo k?” at the 1988 Kalamazoo conference. The bibliography entry is inaccurate; the conjecture's mathematical statement and its 1988 attribution are unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: The bibliography entry `Dean1988` in https://arxiv.org/e-print/2605.02731 cites “Which graphs are pancyclic modulo k?”, Sixth International Conference on the Theory and Applications of Graphs, Kalamazoo, 1988. The publisher's Cycles and Rays record states “Copyright Information: Kluwer Academic Publishers 1990”: https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-94-009-0517-7.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `[De88]` with the Dean reference identified in the cited paper, or rely on the already-listed arXiv Conjecture 1.1 citation. If Cycles and Rays is intended as an alternative source, provide its correct publication year and a precise problem/page reference.

findings.description: The module's `[DeLeSa93]` reference gives the page range 133–139. The paper “Cycles of length 0 modulo 4 in graphs” occupies pages 37–49. This is only a bibliographic error.
findings.source_evidence: The bibliography entry `DLS93` in https://arxiv.org/e-print/2605.02731 gives Discrete Math. 121(1–3):37–49, 1993. Crossref's metadata for DOI 10.1016/0012-365X(93)90535-2 independently confirms that page range.

findings.description: The docstring attributes the k ≥ 6 result to “Liu, Ma and Zhao (2026).” The first author is Luo, not Liu. The formal statement and its solved status are correct.
findings.source_evidence: The author block of “Dean's conjecture and cycles modulo k”, https://arxiv.org/e-print/2601.13552, names Yufan Luo, Jie Ma, and Ziyuan Zhao. Its introduction explicitly resolves Dean's conjecture for all k ≥ 6. The `LMZ2026` bibliography entry in arXiv:2605.02731 also names Y. Luo.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “Liu, Ma and Zhao” with “Luo, Ma and Zhao”; optionally add the arXiv:2601.13552 reference.

https://arxiv.org/e-print/2601.13552 — LaTeX source, authors, introduction, main theorem and following corollary, k = 5 footnote, graph conventions, and bibliography
https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-94-009-0517-7 — publication information and table of contents
Local review guidance: STATEMENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md; historical calibration from /workspace/past_misformalizations/INDEX.md and pr00014.md, pr00574.md, pr01256.md, pr04119.md
review.notes: All seven declarations were checked; no mathematical misformalizations were found. The main conjecture and k = 5 status agree with the cited source, as do the solved cases. The k = 3 and k = 4 declarations intentionally state Dean's special cases, not the stronger surrounding theorems. Scratch files /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/small_cycles.lean compile without errors: they verify the cycle-witness equivalence, empty/edgeless minimum degrees, pointwise degree bounds, nonvacuity, cycle-length bounds, rejection of trivial walks and repeated-vertex circuits, and explicit cycles for k = 3,4,5,6. The older journal full texts were inaccessible through Elsevier, but their relevant results are explicitly quoted in the accessible cited arXiv source; bibliographic metadata was independently checked.
